types.embedding_query_text: PriceTrend Examples: Oil prices, Gas prices, benchmark UK gas price, slowing diesel and petrol prices.

chosen_type.label: PriceTrend
chosen_type.definition: A description of the general direction or movement of prices over a period of time.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a trend in prices; PriceSpecification is the closest concept related to prices, and a trend describes a characteristic of prices over time.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type. Examples: list price, sale price, invoice price, suggested retail price.

candidates.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category. Examples: base price, tax, shipping fee, discount.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: MonetaryAmount perfectly describes a structured value representing a monetary value or range, matching all mentions.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org type directly represents a calendar month as a period; Duration is the most appropriate parent for a standard time period.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: DefinedRegion accurately describes a geographic area like 'Middle East' that is defined by specific, non-administrative criteria.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

chosen_type.label: CommoditySupply
chosen_type.definition: The availability or provision of a raw material or primary agricultural product.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates capture the concept of 'supply' for a commodity; Product is the closest parent as commodities are a type of product.

candidates.label: EnergyConsumptionDetails
candidates.comment: EnergyConsumptionDetails is an Intangible providing information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy, based on international regulations. Also called energy efficiency data, power usage specifications, consumption metrics. Examples: A product's energy label showing kWh/year, details on standby power consumption, information on energy efficiency class.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.

candidates.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.

chosen_type.label: OilBenchmark
chosen_type.definition: A specific grade or type of crude oil used as a standard reference for pricing other oils.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates are relevant to an oil benchmark; Brent crude is a specific type of oil, making Product the most suitable parent.

candidates.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration indicating whether a product is EnergyStar certified. Also called Energy Star rating, Energy Star certification. Examples: EnergyStarCertified, NotEnergyStarCertified.

candidates.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an Enumeration of energy efficiency levels and certifications from various international standards. Also called energy rating, efficiency class, energy certification. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration, EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration.

candidates.label: GasStation
candidates.comment: A GasStation is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells fuel for vehicles. Also called petrol station, filling station, service station. Examples: Shell, ExxonMobil, a local independent gas station.

candidates.label: EngineSpecification
candidates.comment: An EngineSpecification is a StructuredValue providing details about a vehicle's engine. Also called engine details, motor specs, powertrain information. Examples: Engine type (e.g., V6), displacement (e.g., 2.0L), horsepower, fuel type.

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.

chosen_type.label: Percentage
chosen_type.definition: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a simple percentage; Quantity is the appropriate parent for numerical values with units.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValueDistribution is a StructuredValue representing a statistical distribution of values. Also called value distribution, statistical range. Examples: the average height of a population with standard deviation, a product's price distribution across different retailers, a range of test scores with median and mode.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: DayOfWeek is a perfect match for representing a specific day of the week like 'Thursday'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Country Examples: US, Iran, Yemen, Saudi Arabia.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Country is a perfect match for sovereign states and nations listed in the mentions.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: DrugStrength
candidates.comment: A DrugStrength is a MedicalIntangible representing a specific potency in which a medical drug is available in a particular country. Also called medication dosage, pharmaceutical concentration. Examples: "500 mg tablets", "10 mg/mL solution", "25 mcg patch".

chosen_type.label: ParamilitaryGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organization that operates like a military force but is not part of a country's official armed forces.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates fit; a paramilitary group is a type of organization.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: MotorcycleRepair
candidates.comment: An automotive business that provides repair services for motorcycles. Also called motorbike repair shop, motorcycle service center, bike mechanic. Examples: "Joe's Motorcycle Repair", "Custom Bike Service", a local mechanic specializing in motorcycles. Distinct from AutoRepair, which focuses on cars.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: FireStation
candidates.comment: A FireStation is a CivicStructure housing firemen and fire-fighting equipment. Also called fire department, firehouse. Examples: The local city fire station, a volunteer fire department, a regional fire and rescue service.

chosen_type.label: ShipType
chosen_type.definition: A classification or category of waterborne vessels based on their design, purpose, or cargo.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates describe a type of ship; 'oil tankers' are a type of boat/vehicle, making Boat the most specific parent.

candidates.label: ShippingService
candidates.comment: A structured value defining the criteria used to determine if and how an offer can be shipped to a customer. Also called delivery option, shipping method, freight service, courier choice. Examples: 'Standard Ground Shipping', 'Expedited Air Delivery', 'International Economy Shipping'.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: ShippingConditions
candidates.comment: A structured value describing constraints and information about how a product can be shipped, potentially applying to specific product attributes. Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

chosen_type.label: SeaBodyOfWater
chosen_type.justification: SeaBodyOfWater is a precise match for 'Red Sea', which is a large expanse of saltwater.

candidates.label: SeaBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A large expanse of saltwater, typically part of an ocean or a large inland body of saltwater. Also called sea, ocean, marine body, saltwater expanse. Examples: the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, the Black Sea, the Caspian Sea. Distinct from RiverBodyOfWater, which is a flowing freshwater course.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: RiverBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A natural flowing watercourse, typically freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake, or another river. Also called river, stream, waterway, current. Examples: the Nile River, the Amazon River, the Mississippi River, the Thames. Distinct from SeaBodyOfWater, which is a large expanse of saltwater.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

chosen_type.label: TradeRoute
chosen_type.definition: A geographical path or channel regularly used for commercial transport of goods.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a trade route; it is a geographical concept, making Place the most suitable parent.

candidates.label: TradeAction

candidates.label: ShippingConditions

Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.

candidates.label: OfferShippingDetails
candidates.comment: OfferShippingDetails, as a StructuredValue, provides information about shipping destinations, costs, and delivery times for an offer. Also called shipping information, delivery details, postage terms. Examples: 'Free shipping to US', 'Expedited delivery: $15 in 1-2 days', 'International shipping rates vary'. Distinct from OfferItemCondition, which describes the item's state.

candidates.label: RentAction
candidates.comment: RentAction is a TradeAction representing the act of giving money for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object like a vehicle or property. Also called leasing, hiring, renting out. Examples: renting an apartment, leasing a car, hiring a tool, renting a movie.

chosen_type.label: Strait
chosen_type.definition: A narrow, naturally formed navigable waterway that connects two larger bodies of water.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates fit; a strait is a specific type of body of water.

chosen_type.label: LegalContract

chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a general agreement or deal; Contract is a specific type of agreement and a suitable parent.

candidates.label: OfferForLease
candidates.comment: An OfferForLease, as an Offer, represents a proposal to lease out something. Also called lease offer, rental offer, tenancy proposal. Examples: an offer to lease an apartment, a car lease deal, equipment rental terms. Distinct from OfferForPurchase, which is an offer to sell.

candidates.label: OfferItemCondition
candidates.comment: OfferItemCondition is an enumeration listing possible conditions for an item being offered. Also called item state, product condition, quality status. Examples: NewCondition, UsedCondition, RefurbishedCondition, DamagedCondition. Distinct from OfferShippingDetails, which describes shipping logistics.

candidates.label: BorrowAction
candidates.comment: A BorrowAction is a TransferAction representing the act of temporarily obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Also called loan acquisition, temporary possession, rental. Examples: borrowing a library book, renting a car, taking a tool from a friend. Distinct from LendAction, which is the act of giving an object for temporary use.

candidates.label: AgreeAction
candidates.comment: AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent. Examples: Agreeing with a statement, consenting to a proposal, approving a plan, liking a social media post. Distinct from DisagreeAction, which is the act of expressing an inconsistency of opinion.

candidates.label: OfferForPurchase
candidates.comment: An OfferForPurchase, as an Offer, represents a proposal to sell something. Also called sales offer, purchase offer, buy offer. Examples: an offer to sell a house, a product listing on an e-commerce site, a stock offering. Distinct from OfferForLease, which is an offer to rent.

chosen_type.label: Week

candidates.comment: A FinancialService provided by an institution that handles money and credit for customers. Also called bank, credit union, financial institution. Examples: "Chase Bank", "Navy Federal Credit Union", "Citibank". Distinct from AutomatedTeller, which is a machine, not an institution.

chosen_type.label: EventCount
chosen_type.definition: A numerical value representing the total number of occurrences of an event.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a count of events; Quantity is the appropriate parent for numerical values.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org type directly represents a calendar year as a period; Duration is the most appropriate parent for a standard time period.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

chosen_type.label: LegislativeBody
chosen_type.definition: An organization with the power to make or change laws.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent a legislative body; 'Congress' is a type of organization.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicCondition Examples: persistently elevated inflation, price stability.

chosen_type.label: EconomicCondition
chosen_type.definition: The state or status of an economy at a particular time, characterized by various economic indicators.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates broadly cover economic conditions; 'persistently elevated inflation' and 'price stability' are abstract states of the economy, making Intangible appropriate.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A price specification that combines multiple prices applicable for different dimensions of consumption. Also called bundled price, multi-component price, composite pricing. Examples: A utility bill with separate charges for electricity and water, a rental agreement with base rent and a "final cleaning" fee, a software license with per-user and per-feature costs. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general description of a price.

candidates.label: ShippingConditions
candidates.comment: A structured value describing constraints and information about how a product can be shipped, potentially applying to specific product attributes. Also called shipping rules, delivery terms, freight conditions, shipping policy. Examples: free shipping for orders over $50, express shipping for lightweight items, international shipping restrictions.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicPolicy Examples: reductions in borrowing costs.

chosen_type.label: EconomicPolicy
chosen_type.definition: A course of action taken by a government to influence the economy.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidates represent an economic policy; 'reductions in borrowing costs' is an abstract policy, making Intangible the appropriate parent.

candidates.label: RepaymentSpecification
candidates.comment: A RepaymentSpecification is a StructuredValue representing the details of a repayment. Also called repayment terms, loan repayment details, amortization schedule. Examples: a mortgage repayment schedule, the terms for a credit card payment, details of a student loan repayment plan, a payment installment plan.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: LoanOrCredit
candidates.comment: A financial product representing an amount of money loaned or a line of credit offered under specific terms and charges. Also called credit facility, lending product, financial loan. Examples: a personal loan, a credit card, a mortgage, a business line of credit. Distinct from MortgageLoan, which is specifically a loan secured by real estate.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: MortgageLoan
candidates.comment: A loan or credit product where property or real estate is used as collateral. Also called home loan, property loan, real estate financing. Examples: a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, a variable-rate home loan, a commercial property mortgage. Distinct from LoanOrCredit, which is a general loan and not necessarily secured by real estate.

chosen_type.label: ConferenceEvent
chosen_type.justification: ConferenceEvent is a suitable fit as a meeting is a type of event involving discussions, similar to a conference.

candidates.label: MeetingRoom
candidates.comment: A room within an accommodation, such as a hotel, provided for singular events like business conferences and meetings. Also called conference room, conference hall, boardroom, event space. Examples: a hotel's grand ballroom, a corporate meeting room, a small seminar room. Distinct from Room, which is a general category for any room.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: JoinAction
candidates.comment: A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action. Examples: joining a club, attending a meeting, becoming a member of a team. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is signing up for a service, and SubscribeAction, which implies receiving updates.

candidates.label: BefriendAction
candidates.comment: An InteractAction representing the act of forming a mutual personal connection with someone. Also called make friends with, become friends, form a friendship. Examples: "Befriending a new colleague", "Making friends with a neighbor", "Forming a bond with a classmate". Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a non-reciprocal connection.
